subject: Chain-of-custody transfer steps for incident 2028-01-18
messages:
From: Elena Park <security@acmehealth.com>
To: Logan Wright <logan_wright@redwood.ai>
Cc: Jon Freedman <jon.freedman@forensica.io>
Date: Thu, 18 Jan 2028 09:12:00 -0800
Subject: Request: Preserve and transfer analysis artifacts (Incident ACME-2028-01)

Hi Logan,

Following the suspicious access window we discussed, Acme is requesting Redwood preserve the relevant runtime logs, trace artifacts, and a minimal set of request payloads for Forensica's analysis. We need:

- All inference request/response logs for the window 2028-01-16 22:00 to 2028-01-17 03:00 UTC (including KV cache IDs).
- Any debug traces or worker-level stderr captured for that period.
- Linkable manifest with SHA256 digests for each exported file.

Two asks: please (1) confirm the retention hold and the earliest ETA for a secure export; (2) outline the chain-of-custody transfer steps so our legal/compliance team can sign off. Jon from Forensica is on copy.

Attached: acme_preserve_request.pdf (request letter).

Thanks — Elena
Elena Park
Head of Security, Acme Health
security@acmehealth.com

From: Logan Wright <logan_wright@redwood.ai>
To: Elena Park <security@acmehealth.com>
Cc: Marissa Cole <marissa_cole@redwood.ai>, Monica Patel <monica_patel@redwood.ai>, Karthik Iyer <karthik_iyer@redwood.ai>, Jon Freedman <jon.freedman@forensica.io>
Date: Thu, 18 Jan 2028 09:25:00 -0800
Subject: Re: Request: Preserve and transfer analysis artifacts (Incident ACME-2028-01)

Elena — thanks for the clear ask and the attached letter. Short answers up front: we will place a temporary legal/forensic hold immediately and can produce a secured export within 24 hours; below I've sketched the chain-of-custody (CoC) flow and ETA assumptions.

High-level CoC flow (initial):
1) Hold: create a named hold "ACME-2028-01-HOLD" scoped to the requested time window and artifact types.
2) Export staging: snapshot artifacts to an encrypted S3 bucket in Redwood's evidence partition (us-west-2) using server-side KMS key wrap.
3) Manifest: generate export_manifest_20280118.csv w/ file paths, sizes, and SHA256 hashes.
4) Transfer: provide access via pre-signed, single-use URLs and optional Aspera/HTTPs to Forensica.
5) Acknowledgement: Forensica to sign the CoC template and return signed DocuSign reference.

Assumptions and constraints:
- Exports will be region-bound (us-west-2) unless Acme requests cross-region escrow.
- We will not include raw customer PII fields unless explicitly requested and authorized in writing.
- We will retain the hold for 90 days by default, after which we will follow the deletion trigger below unless Acme extends.

I'll put Marissa and Monica on the operational steps, and Karthik to confirm preservation scope and hashing mechanics.

Next: Marissa, Monica — can you confirm estimated wall time for snapshot + manifest and whether we need a dedicated GPU pool snapshot to collect worker-level stderr?

Thanks,
Logan Wright
Senior Incident Manager, Redwood Inference

From: Marissa Cole <marissa_cole@redwood.ai>
To: Logan Wright <logan_wright@redwood.ai>, Elena Park <security@acmehealth.com>
Cc: Monica Patel <monica_patel@redwood.ai>, Karthik Iyer <karthik_iyer@redwood.ai>, Jon Freedman <jon.freedman@forensica.io>
Date: Thu, 18 Jan 2028 10:01:00 -0800
Subject: Re: Request: Preserve and transfer analysis artifacts (Incident ACME-2028-01)

Thanks — quick operational plan from my side.

Workplan (detailed):
- 10:15: Create ACME-2028-01-HOLD in the retention service; annotate policy with scope tags (runtime-logs, traces, kv-ids).
- 10:30–12:00: Run export job: incremental snapshot of S3/Hotstore + zipped worker logs. We will perform manifest hashing (SHA256) per file and compute an overall bundle Merkle root to include in the PDF CoC.
- 12:00–12:15: Stage export to s3://evidence-exports/redwood/acme/2028-01-18-0900Z/ (server-side-encrypted with KMS key alias rwf-evidence-usw2).
- 12:15–12:30: Generate export_manifest_20280118.csv (filename, path, size, sha256, originating-node-id).
- 12:30–12:45: Run integrity check and package CoC template (chain_of_custody_template.docx) with bundle SHA256 + timestamped signature.
- 12:45–13:00: Create time-limited pre-signed URLs and DocuSign envelope for Acme.

Security notes:
- Exported archives will be encrypted with envelope keys; private key material is HSM-wrapped.
- Access logs to the export bucket will be retained and included in the manifest (who accessed which object and when).

Open question for legal: do we need a notary/third-party witness for the transfer or is DocuSign-signed CoC sufficient for Acme's compliance team?

ETA: first secure link to Forensica by 12:55 PT (today).

— Marissa
Marissa Cole
Platform Reliability Lead, Redwood Inference

From: Jon Freedman <jon.freedman@forensica.io>
To: Marissa Cole <marissa_cole@redwood.ai>, Elena Park <security@acmehealth.com>
Cc: Logan Wright <logan_wright@redwood.ai>, Monica Patel <monica_patel@redwood.ai>, Karthik Iyer <karthik_iyer@redwood.ai>
Date: Thu, 18 Jan 2028 12:34:00 -0800
Subject: Re: Request: Preserve and transfer analysis artifacts (Incident ACME-2028-01)

Marissa / Team — thanks for the rapid plan. DocuSign-signed CoC + manifest with SHA256 digests is acceptable for Acme's e-discovery workflow. A couple of practical asks from Forensica:

1) Please include worker node identifiers (or container IDs) in the manifest so we can correlate runtime traces to process dumps.
2) If possible, provide a compressed text index of request IDs (no full request bodies) so we can request a bounded subset later.
3) Confirm whether the pre-signed links are single-use or multi-access, and whether they expire after first download.

We will sign and return the CoC as soon as we receive the DocuSign envelope. Once we pull the bundle we will validate hashes and send an acknowledgment email with our chain-of-custody receipt.

— Jon Freedman
Lead Forensic Analyst, Forensica
jon.freedman@forensica.io

From: Logan Wright <logan_wright@redwood.ai>
To: Elena Park <security@acmehealth.com>, Jon Freedman <jon.freedman@forensica.io>
Cc: Marissa Cole <marissa_cole@redwood.ai>, Monica Patel <monica_patel@redwood.ai>, Karthik Iyer <karthik_iyer@redwood.ai>
Date: Thu, 18 Jan 2028 14:05:00 -0800
Subject: Re: Request: Preserve and transfer analysis artifacts (Incident ACME-2028-01)

Elena / Jon — final status update:

- Hold created: ACME-2028-01-HOLD (retention flagged, 90-day default).
- Export staged: s3://evidence-exports/redwood/acme/2028-01-18-0900Z/ (files listed in export_manifest_20280118.csv).
- Attachments posted to Drive and DocuSign envelope sent (DocuSign ID: 0f4e2b-ACME-EVIDENCE-AGREEMENT).
- Pre-signed URLs: single-use, 24-hour TTL by default. We can change to 72 hours if Acme prefers.
- Worker identifiers and container IDs included in manifest as originating-node-id. A compressed request ID index (index_request_ids.txt.gz) is included but not containing request bodies.

Next steps for Acme: please sign the DocuSign CoC; Forensica to pull and validate bundle, then send signed receipt to evidence@redwood.ai. After 90 days the bundle will be purged unless an extension is requested in writing.

If Acme needs cross-region escrow (EU residency), open a ticket and we'll schedule a secure escrow transfer window (this requires additional approvals and a custodian agreement).

Closing note: we flagged the export with an immutable manifest and HSM-wrapped keys; we will retain an access audit trails export for 365 days.

Logan Wright
Senior Incident Manager, Redwood Inference
